analysis: The trial crashed with a nonzero train.py exit after consuming 5.12 allocated GPU-seconds. No validation score was produced, so history fusion’s effect on the reported 0.59 reference is unknown. The supplied traceback shows only the worker’s subprocess failure; it omits the underlying training exception and does not establish the cause or whether diagnostics completed. This is an execution failure, not evidence against the architecture.
code_summary: One jointly optimized model per category combines 3-layer, 64-dimensional LightGCN with attention over the latest 128 preceding items. Attention uses propagated item vectors, learned relative positions, and a graph-user query; a learned gate initialized toward the graph user fuses both representations. Scores use tied propagated item embeddings and a jointly trained item bias. Training samples sequence cut points, uses 64 negatives excluding all observed training items, and retains the full-training transductive graph. Empty histories preserve the graph user; unknown users use the same encoder with a zero user vector. The predictor writer routes all four datasets and strictly loads one selected checkpoint per category. Checkpoint selection uses validation HR@10 with NDCG@10 tie-breaking; no averaging or ensemble is implemented.
